definitions.explanation: An inherent quality or attribute that distinguishes something from others. Often used in technical and academic contexts for the properties of materials, devices, or natural phenomena.

examples.japanese: この{素材|そざい}の{特性|とくせい}を{調|しら}べる。
examples.english: To examine the properties of this material.

examples.japanese: {地域|ちいき}の{特性|とくせい}を{生|い}かした{商品|しょうひん}{開発|かいはつ}が{進|すす}んでいる。
examples.english: Product development that leverages the distinctive characteristics of the region is progressing.

examples.japanese: この{薬|くすり}は{水|みず}に{溶|と}けやすいという{特性|とくせい}を{持|も}っている。
examples.english: This medicine has the characteristic of being easily soluble in water.

notes:
USAGE:
{特性|とくせい} emphasizes inherent, distinguishing properties — qualities that are built-in rather than acquired. It is more technical than {特徴|とくちょう} (feature, characteristic), which describes any noticeable trait. {特性|とくせい} is preferred when discussing material properties, device specifications, or scientific attributes.

Note: The homophone {特製|とくせい} (specially made) is a different word.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {特性|とくせい}を{生|い}かす: to make use of characteristics
- {特性|とくせい}を{持|も}つ: to have a property
- {材料|ざいりょう}の{特性|とくせい}: material properties
- {電気|でんき}{特性|とくせい}: electrical characteristics
- {特性|とくせい}を{分析|ぶんせき}する: to analyze properties
